The Old Pensioner

He sits upon the park bench grey,
Watching the children run and play.
His coat is worn, his eyes are dim,
The world has little time for him.
Once he marched with strength and pride,
With comrades marching by his side.
Now silence is his only friend,
Waiting for the journey's end.
The autumn leaves drift softly down,
Like golden tears upon the town.

The Storm

The sky turned a bruised purple as the wind began to howl like a wounded animal. Trees bent in submission, their branches scraping the ground in a desperate plea for mercy. Amaka hurriedly gathered the drying clothes, her wrapper whipping furiously around her legs. Thunder rumbled, a deep, angry growl from the belly of the clouds, followed by a blinding flash that tore the sky apart. It was not just a rainstorm; it was nature declaring war on the village.
